recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If this enforcement regresses, fix or version the external Kindling/Publisher tooling rather than adding redundant core prose or editing generated artifacts in HL7/fhir.
issue_request: FHIR-10292 was Published/Persuasive and asked that the build fail when an element of type code has a binding strength other than required, copied from the Condition.clinicalStatus code/preferred example in FHIR-10272.
initial_application: HL7/fhir commit 25a14c34669e6e4e477a6970231743ce1ebd9432 ('#10292 - check bindings properly') matches the Jira SVN revision comment and changed the then-vendored ResourceValidator to require simple code bindings to be required, allow a max-binding exception, and require code elements to provide bindings.
additional_context: FHIR-10272 fixed the original Condition.clinicalStatus example; current active Condition source has clinicalStatus as CodeableConcept with a required ConditionClinicalStatus binding. FHIR-28285 later reaffirmed and refined the same tooling rule, including the max-binding/extensible exception, and is already represented on the combined branch by 06449f181d7b733debe269c563625ba4ca0e0e4c. Current HL7/fhir delegates publisher validation to org.hl7.fhir:kindling.
reconciliation: No HL7/fhir source file was changed. The active implementation is in external HL7/kindling ResourceValidator, and scans of current StructureDefinition XML and spreadsheet source found no code element bindings with non-required strength.

related_jiras.note: Original Condition.clinicalStatus report that supplied the concrete code/preferred example and requested both a source fix and build-tool enforcement.
Later Published/Persuasive FHIR-I issue reaffirming code binding enforcement and the max-binding/extensible exception; already audited on the combined branch.
